corrected_value.title: Relation of promoter methylation of the structural oxytocin gene to critical life events in major depression: A case control study

decision.quote: Recently, we found hypomethylation of OXT in patients with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) compared to healthy controls (HC). Since the replicability of findings is a key point of criticism in (epi‑)genetic research, we aimed to confirm our previous findings in a pre-registered study (data was stored in a database prior to pre-registration) within a new sample of n = 85 patients with MDD and n = 85 HC.
decision.location: Current primary Abstract; complete deposited references and independently verified original reports0121
decision.reason: Apply Step2 description matching to the actual reported finding, not to hypothetical unseen analyses. The current85MDD/85HC abstract explicitly retests prior OXT hypomethylation in MDD versus healthy controls. Within its complete deposited references, the JAD2020case-control article at821has a primary-author abstract explicitly reporting this finding in90MDD/90HC. The other2020OXT article abstract reports146MDD inpatients and within-patient stress/severity/sex analyses, not the specified HC contrast;2021SLC6A4is a different gene. Thus only the JAD report positively fits the described empirical contrast under the available primary evidence. Select already shipped821by description. This does not claim that an inaccessible other body contains no secondary control analysis or that every2024finding is attributed; current in-text attribution remains unavailable. The final expert uncertainty rests on a merely possible hidden analysis rather than a second positively equally fitting reported finding and is explicitly superseded. No extra original or missing pair is created.

corrected_value.title: Academic and Behavior Combined Support: Evaluation of an integrated supplemental intervention for early elementary students

decision.quote: The purpose of this research was to conduct a practice-based replication of Academic and Behavior Combined Support (ABC Support), a previously developed and experimentally evaluated supplemental intervention that merges a combined focus on reading fluency and academic engagement.
decision.location: Current primary Abstract; complete deposited references and independently verified original reports0121
decision.reason: The current4-student Grade2practice-based replication describes an earlier experimentally evaluated ABC Support intervention and repeats reading-fluency/engagement/disruption outcomes. Complete original-source inspection establishes the2021JSP article at1563as the empirical evaluation, with six teacher-student dyads, randomized multiple baseline and reported outcome changes. The second ABC Support reference,2022Intervention in School and Clinic, is complete practitioner implementation guidance with10elements/15steps and no empirical study sample/design/outcome analysis. Step2 therefore uniquely selects the2021evaluation by description. No same-dataset equivalence is inferred. The raw expert reason incorrectly attributes a five-author guidance citation including Schienebeck; the actual inspected online-first guidance author block is Gettinger/Kratochwill/Foy/Eubanks. That author-list claim is not adopted. The selected2021five-author empirical citation is independently supported. No source-body completeness or analytic equivalence is inferred for the unavailable2024body.
